novelty_flags.one_line: Tier=subfield below novelty_target=field: the survey omits exact rational min-cost-flow/transport certification (notably Orlin1993), so the stated certificate output has no demonstrated advantage over an established exact primal-dual route; a field claim needs a Sinkhorn-specific asymptotic, verification, or causal-decision advantage.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper rounds an approximately scaled Sinkhorn matrix to an exactly feasible coupling and proves an additive upper approximation to discrete linear OT; its stated main complexity initially counts arithmetic operations and Remark 1 only discusses bit complexity briefly.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Lemma 10 as reproduced in the proceedings PDF
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings paper studies approximate matrix scaling, including error in marginal computations; Lemma 10 bounds the scale of approximate Sinkhorn updates under a stated fixed-point precision budget.

The paper characterizes convergent concave annealing schedules and separates entropic and marginal-relaxation errors on the regularization path; it analyzes convergence rather than a rational outward original-value certificate.

The preprint studies marginal-only partially identified GMM through support-function OT, entropic regularization, a CLT, bootstrap inference, and applications including attrition and refreshment samples.
The paper proves explicit nonasymptotic convergence of entropy-penalized linear programs to the original linear-program optimum, including matching lower bounds.
The paper constructs estimators and confidence regions for minimizer/identified sets by inversion of a sample criterion and develops consistency and rates.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:0805.1971 preprint corresponding to JASA article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs finite-sample multinomial confidence regions through inversion of covering collections associated with likelihood level sets.

The paper gives a strongly polynomial minimum-cost-flow algorithm. Rational two-marginal discrete OT is a transportation/minimum-cost-flow instance, so its exact primal-dual value certificate is the necessary baseline for the proposed output claim.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: State and prove a Sinkhorn-specific advantage over exact min-cost flow: permit variable I and J, specify a near-linear or otherwise superior bit-work bound, and retain an independently checkable original-value lower bound after transcendental rounding and exact repair.

Add an explicit reduction from a named marginal-only causal model, such as the Franguridi–Liu attrition/refreshment setting, to a certificate decision whose outcome cannot be supplied by a generic LP solver without losing a stated computational or auditability guarantee.

Replace the broad seven-clause OEQ with a worked nontrivial variable-dimension family and a direct theorem-level comparison against a rational min-cost-flow primal-dual certificate, identifying the precise resource or verification property that Sinkhorn improves.

recommended_next_step: Revise the flagship kernel around a demonstrable Sinkhorn-specific advantage over exact rational transportation/min-cost-flow certification; otherwise demote the project to a software-engineering implementation note.
